9.  Agreement for Temporary  Assistant to the City Manager Ranells reported on the agreement for
  Employment( Anthony Ciotti)  temporary employment  with  Anthony Ciotti. He stated that Deputy Director of
  Public Works Anthony Ciotti has submitted paperwork to retire after a long
  career in public service with him serving the City of La Verne for 13 years. Due
  to unfortunate circumstances, the City' s Fleet Manager position is currently
  vacant leaving a substantial gap. One of the many roles Mr. Ciotti has had as
  the Deputy Director of Public Works was overseeing fleet division operations.
  The City is interested in retaining Mr. Ciotti' s services to fill the City' s current
  gap as the interim Fleet Manager while a recruitment process for a permanent
  replacement  is completed.  In order to be compliant with California Law and
  the 2013 Pension Reform Act, it is necessary for the City Council to certify
  there is an urgent need to waive the 180- day waiting period as well as take an
  action affirming the execution of such employment arrangements. Resolution
  No. 21-  45 and the agreement satisfy those requirements.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter.

  There was none.

  The City Council was appreciative of Mr. Ciotti willingness to fill the position of
  Fleet Manager until one was hired. They agreed he is a loyal and hard worker.

  It was moved by Davis, seconded by Crosby, and unanimously carried by roll
  call to approve Resolution No. 21- 45, authorizing the City Manager to execute
  an agreement with Anthony Ciotti to provide temporary, part- time employment.

10.  White Ave. Storm Drain Pipe  Public Works Director Igoe reported on the White Avenue storm drain pipe
  Replacement Necessitated  by  replacement necessitated by Gold Line Construction. He stated that Kiewit
  Gold  Line Construction  Parsons Joint Venture ( KPJV) is continuing with their advancements on
  construction efforts related to the Metro Gold Line( now Metro L Line) light rail
  project. As part of the work, various utility improvements were needed for
  water; sewer and storm drain lines with much of this utility work having been
  completed thus far. However, finro 24" storm drain lines previously believed to
  be owned by Southern California Regional Rail Authority ( SCRRA, aka
  Metrolink) are now believed to be owned by the City of La Verne and require
  replacement. Staff therefor recommends these pipes be replaced by KPJV
  versus independent construction contracts due to this being time sensitive and
  there being a cost saving of KPJV being mobilized and available to complete
  the needed work.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter.

  There was  one  phone  communication.  (  To hear what was said during public
  comment,  please  visit  the City' s website to view the archived Council meeting).
   City Council Minutes, Tuesday, July 6, 2021,  Page 5,

  It was moved by Crosby, seconded by and unanimously carried by roll call to
  appropriate $  391, 772 from the Storm Drain Fund ( 419) to replace two 24"
  corrugated metal storm drain pipes on White Avenue within the Metrolink right-
  of- way.

11.  Approval  of a  Standards  of  City Manager Russi reported on the request for approval of a Standards of
  Cover Analysis/ Community  Cover Analysis/Community Risk Assessment. He stated that a request for
  Risk Assessment  quote of a Standards of Coverage Analysis and Community Risk Assessment
  SOC/ CRA) was sent to three reputable firms. The document was necessary
  to provide the City and Department current objective data which will be used to
  compare our existing service delivery model to the industry standard and the
  future fire service  needs  for the City of La Verne.  He stated that AP Triton was
  found to be a qualified and experienced consulting firm and he recommended
  that the City Council approve an agreement with AP Triton to provide the City
  of La Verne with a Standards of Cover( SOC) and Community Risk
  Assessment( CRA) Analysis of the City' s Fire and Emergency Medical service
  operations and to approve funding.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter.

  There was none.

  The City Council discussed the timeline for completion of the SOC report and
  that they looked forward to receiving the data.

  It was moved by Carder, seconded by Lau, and unanimously carried by roll call
  to authorize the City Manager to execute an agreement with AP Triton, a
  qualified and experienced consulting firm to provide the City of La Verne with a
  Standards of Cover( SOC) and Community Risk Assessment( CRA) Analysis
  of the City' s Fire and Emergency Medical service operations.

  Mayor Pro Tem Davis reported that the July Pomona Valley Transportation
  Committee meeting was canceled due to a lack of business. He stated that the
  July Cultural Awareness Social Inclusion Committee(  CASI) meeting  was also
  cancelled. He reported on attending the La Verne Coalition of Concerned
  Citizens ( LV3C) meeting. He stated that the Fourth of July parade was
  spectacular.  He thanked Council Members Carder and Lau, the Fourth of July
  Committee and City staff for their hard work on the parade. He hoped
  everyone had a good time and that everyone enjoyed the fireworks show and
  hoped for the continuation  of a good year.

  Council Member Lau also thanked the Fourth of July Committee and City staff
  for their hard work  on  the parade.  She stated it took a lot of patience,  a lot of
  hard work  and  dedication to make the FourthJuly  of  celebration  happen.  She
  thanked the La Verne Retired Senior Volunteers( RSVP) and the many
  volunteers who helped on that day. She urged everyone to stay safe, to
  continue to wash your hands, and to be kind to each other.

  Council Member Crosby recognized and thanked Jeff Blasser and Tim
  Morrison for Fourth of July Patriotic Motorcycle salute ride in the parade.  He

  thanked City staff and stated it was a great Fourth of July.

  Mayor Hepburn also thanked everyone involved for the outstanding job on the
  Fourth of July parade and fireworks show. He reported on the installation of
  Morgan Sternquist as the new chair to the La Verne Chamber of Commerce.
  He reported on the upcoming Community Yard Sale.
